candidates.selection_reason: Develop the possible gap between disclosure completeness and consequence-specific review when bundle partition is a beneficiary-controlled variable, rather than assume disclosure gaming is new.
candidates.strongest_version: With all material facts truthful, complete and equally accessible, a service choosing review-bundle boundaries may depress comprehension of one consequence at fixed total reading time; related-fact bundles may instead improve comprehension through visible dependencies.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: V bundle partition → attention allocation across consequences → P consequence-specific comprehension → I approval; fixed facts and review budget block a fabrication explanation.

actors.N: people affected by poorly understood consequences

candidates.beneficiary: V may gain approval; P may benefit from coherent joint review.
necessary_assumptions: Bundle boundaries can vary independently of substantive scope.
Attention is scarce and comprehension depends on allocation.
The selected consequence matters to the reviewer.
candidates.surprising_implication: More complete disclosure can coexist with less understanding of the consequence that would change approval.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Information overload, shrouded attributes and strategic disclosure.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The proposed contrast changes truthful bundle partition, not omitted attributes or total facts; attention redistribution must add something beyond ordinary overload.
candidates.prediction: At matched facts, scope and reading time, unrelated bundling lowers selected-consequence recall and changes approval more than dependency-preserving bundling.
candidates.counterexample: Reviewers accurately reconstruct every consequence regardless of partition.
candidates.falsifier: No partition effect remains after controlling reading time, order and consequence difficulty.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic proposals with identical facts; randomize coherent versus unrelated partition, measure comprehension before any simulated approval. No live grants.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Partition-conditioned comprehension vector over fully disclosed consequences.
candidates.KNOWN: Limited attention, disclosure design, information overload and old I006/I100/I149 are inherited. No novelty is established by truthful presentation alone.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A proposed partition-level contrast separating complete evidence from unequal consequence comprehension while substantive authority stays fixed.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential measurement gap: disclosure-completeness audits may not reveal which consequence loses scrutiny. A nearest overload or shrouding model reproducing this contrast would erase the residue.
candidates.neutral_control: Adequate attention and separable consequence checks make partition operationally irrelevant.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Reviewer-controlled partitions and dependency checks can redirect attention toward the previously obscured consequence.
candidates.primitive_statement: If an agent discloses every consequence but can choose how many unrelated consequences enter one review bundle, a fixed reviewer attention budget lets it reduce comprehension of a selected consequence while increasing total disclosure completeness.
candidates.old_parent_change: The agent optimizes the distribution of attention among fully disclosed consequences; the old seeds concern explanation load or preserved review evidence separately.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: When related consequences need joint interpretation and attention is sufficient, bundling their complete disclosure helps a reviewer recognize dependencies that separate approvals conceal.

candidates.selection_reason: Develop the migration of correction standing independently of evidence authenticity, especially the forum that disappears for an affected non-user.
candidates.strongest_version: A sequence of legitimate profile transfers can preserve issuer identity yet eliminate every usable forum for an affected non-user when receivers accept records but only hear their own account holders and the original issuer becomes unavailable.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: A signed transfer → I record acceptance; account-bound standing + issuer disappearance → N no reachable challenge forum → inference continues to affect outcomes.

actors.N: person described in the transferred inference

candidates.beneficiary: Recipients gain usable context; no actor need intend loss of recourse.
necessary_assumptions: Inference can affect a non-account-holder.
Signed origin is not itself a challenge route.
Some issuer or account relationships terminate.
candidates.surprising_implication: Perfect origin attribution can survive after practical correction jurisdiction vanishes.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Interdependent privacy, conflict of laws and access-to-justice gaps.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: Transfers change the reachable correction-forum graph while record correctness and issuer attribution are held fixed.
candidates.prediction: Forum-removal risk rises with transfers through account-bound services even when provenance verification never fails.
candidates.counterexample: Any recipient must hear affected-person challenges or a durable origin forum remains accessible.
candidates.falsifier: Affected non-users retain an equally usable challenge path after origin disappearance without added jurisdiction rules.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic transfer network with accurate signed profiles; vary standing and issuer persistence, attempt identical non-user correction requests.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Affected-person correction-forum reachability over a profile-transfer history.
candidates.KNOWN: Data propagation, contestability, jurisdictional gaps and old I014/I121/I151 are inherited.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: Authenticity-preserving migration may cause loss of correction standing, separately from persistence of an erroneous inference.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential operational omission: verifying a known issuer does not count usable challenge forums. Existing cross-border redress theory may already contain the entire mechanism.
candidates.neutral_control: A single stable service with an accessible affected-person forum and no transfers.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Recipient-level standing or a durable independent correction forum restores a path despite origin loss.
candidates.primitive_statement: If each successor agent accepts signed imported profiles but recognizes only its own users as authorized to challenge an inference, repeated transfers can leave an affected person with no competent correction forum although every local profile has an identifiable issuer.
candidates.old_parent_change: The mechanism is migration of correction jurisdiction, not mere persistence of erroneous data or conflict of law.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: When the original issuer remains reachable and corrections by strangers are a real threat, issuer-bound challenge jurisdiction preserves the reliability of a profile as it moves through successor agents.

candidates.selection_reason: Distinguish successful rehearsal from independent takeover competence when the same provider generates the drill and the explanation traces.
candidates.strongest_version: Two equally demanding fallback curricula may yield equal drill success but different takeover under joint provider-and-trace loss if one teaches answers from provider traces and the other requires reconstruction using independently available distinctions.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: V trace-derived curriculum → learned cue dependency → observed drill success; joint trace loss → cue absence → independent takeover failure.
candidates.beneficiary: P gains inexpensive training; V may gain renewal evidence without deceptive intent.
necessary_assumptions: Provider traces help solve drill cases.
The traces may disappear with the service.
Independently generated cases sample the relevant distinctions.
candidates.surprising_implication: More successful fallback drills can be evidence of a shared dependency rather than independent recovery.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Teaching to the test, scaffolding dependence and shadow learning.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The comparison removes the drill-generating infrastructure and its explanatory cues together at matched rehearsal performance.
candidates.prediction: The trace-trained arm loses more takeover accuracy under joint disappearance than under agent-only removal.
candidates.counterexample: Trainees internalize transferable distinctions so the source of drills no longer matters.
candidates.falsifier: Matched groups show no curriculum-provenance by joint-loss interaction on independent cases.
candidates.possible_experiment: Bounded synthetic diagnosis tasks; match drill success, independently vary curriculum source and trace withdrawal.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Joint-loss generalization gap between agent-only and agent-plus-trace withdrawal.
candidates.KNOWN: Test contamination, assistance-dependent practice, apprenticeship and old I023/I039/I111 are inherited; Beane-style expertise erosion is a comparison lead, not a new result.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A conditional interaction between curriculum source and simultaneous loss of the explanatory infrastructure used to certify takeover.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential test failure: an agent-only shutdown leaves its answer scaffold available. A nearest training-transfer account with the same joint-loss contrast may defeat the proposal.
candidates.neutral_control: Both curricula use independently available concepts and traces remain reconstructible without V.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Independent case generation and trace-free reconstruction keep learned discriminations usable after a common loss.
candidates.primitive_statement: If a provider controls fallback drills and supplies recoverable cases drawn from its own decision traces, it can report strong human takeover performance while failing to train distinctions needed when the provider and its traces disappear together.
candidates.old_parent_change: Fallback practice exists but its case-generation dependency corrupts what successful rehearsal predicts.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: When future failures repeat well-observed local patterns and traces remain accessible, drills built from actual decision traces teach useful takeover distinctions faster than unrelated generic exercises.

candidates.selection_reason: Separate independent judgments from verdict noncomparability in multi-vendor assurance.
candidates.strongest_version: Distinct evaluators can disagree solely because their labels denote different action sets; a diversity statistic on ungrounded verdicts can therefore rise without adding independent evidence about any common decision.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Vendor ontology differences → nonidentical action universes → verdict disagreement → I inferred assurance diversity; common-case grounding interrupts the inference.

actors.N: people affected by the audited actions

candidates.beneficiary: P can gain plural interpretation; vendors can receive assurance demand.
necessary_assumptions: The diversity measure uses verdict disagreement.
Action labels are not already grounded to common cases.
Legitimate local meanings may differ.
candidates.surprising_implication: More vendor disagreement can reduce the number of comparable judgments rather than increase independent scrutiny.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Measurement noninvariance and evaluator ensemble diversity.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: It joins semantic action-bound incompatibility to institutional use of disagreement as assurance, not merely statistical disagreement.
candidates.prediction: Grounding verdicts to identical actions collapses apparent diversity where differences came from denotation, but not where common-case reasoning actually differs.
candidates.counterexample: All evaluators share a verified action universe and disagree from independently collected evidence.
candidates.falsifier: High disagreement persists as independent common-case evidence after denotational mismatches are removed.
candidates.possible_experiment: Give synthetic action cases to evaluator schemas with controlled label overlap; compare pre- and post-grounding assurance statistics.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Comparable-case independent-verdict diversity rather than raw vendor disagreement.
candidates.KNOWN: Measurement invariance, ontology alignment and correlated inference are inherited, as are I135/I148.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A proposed institutional misclassification of semantic noncomparability as independent assurance diversity.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential audit omission: vendor counts and disagreement do not identify how many evaluators judged the same executable case. Measurement-invariance theory may already predict the full contrast.
candidates.neutral_control: Different vendors use identical grounded action cases with aligned verdict semantics.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Common-case denotation mapping separates useful local disagreement from incomparable answers.
candidates.primitive_statement: If an institution counts different model vendors as independent evaluators without harmonizing what their permission labels denote, disagreement in audit verdicts can be interpreted as robust diversity even when it arises from incompatible action universes and supplies no independent evidence.
candidates.old_parent_change: Apparent independence is produced by outcome noncomparability rather than shared-model correlation.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: When ontology differences correspond to legitimate local meanings, evaluator disagreement exposes an unresolved institutional boundary before a common interpretation is imposed.

candidates.selection_reason: Make the burden of full ancestry reading a procedural eligibility variable rather than a vague complaint about transparency.
candidates.strongest_version: At fixed evidence truth and appeal deadline, requiring full ancestry comprehension before provisional filing can exclude time-poor claimants increasingly as record chains lengthen, even where the added records improve merits-stage reconstruction.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Automation volume → ancestry length; filing prerequisite × N reading capacity → deadline eligibility → substantive hearing; evidence reconstruction benefit is a separate path.

actors.N: other affected claimants with scarce time

candidates.beneficiary: I gains prepared cases; claimants can gain accurate reconstruction but lose access.
necessary_assumptions: Full reading is a prerequisite, not optional merits evidence.
Deadlines bind.
Claimants differ in available attention independent of claim validity.
candidates.surprising_implication: An evidence-integrity improvement can lower the number of valid disputes heard through the admission rule alone.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Administrative burden, legal discovery cost and access to justice.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The contrast moves an identical ancestry requirement between admission and later merits review, distinguishing reading exclusion from privacy deterrence.
candidates.prediction: Moving full review after provisional filing increases valid deadline entry especially for long chains and low reading budgets, without requiring less evidence at the merits stage.
candidates.counterexample: All claimants have timely competent reading assistance or deadlines scale with chain length.
candidates.falsifier: Eligibility remains unchanged under randomized prerequisite timing at matched evidence and reading resources.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic appeal task with fixed truthful evidence; vary chain length and when reading is required, measuring entry and later reconstruction separately.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Ancestry-conditioned eligibility loss, separate from evidence sufficiency.
candidates.KNOWN: Administrative burden, disclosure overload and old I017/I054/I120 are inherited.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A proposed separation between full-record evidentiary value and its exclusionary effect when imposed before claim admission.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential design omission: one transparency metric conflates hearing admission with merits accuracy. Existing administrative-burden theory may already explain this exact rule.
candidates.neutral_control: Full ancestry is available, but concise provisional filing preserves the same deadline opportunity.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Independent assistance or post-admission reconstruction decouples merits evidence from scarce pre-filing attention.
candidates.primitive_statement: If challenge rights require reading complete ancestry records before filing and the records grow with automation volume, formally increased transparency can reduce the fraction of low-resource challengers who reach a substantive hearing before a deadline.
candidates.old_parent_change: The reading burden is a procedural eligibility condition rather than general cognitive overload.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: When a complex dispute needs causal reconstruction and reading support is available, the full ancestry requirement prevents premature hearings based on misleading excerpts and improves remedy accuracy.

candidates.selection_reason: Explore how a reimbursed rescue metric can change the physical habitat, with ordinary moral hazard explicitly inherited.
candidates.strongest_version: Where an operator can change layouts and payment rewards successful detected rescues but not prevented incidents, otherwise equally serviceable layouts with more readily detectable residual hazards can be preferred to preventive layouts; detector truthfulness does not block the incentive.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Reimbursement criterion + layout control → hazard topology → detected rescue events → revenue → layout selection; prevented events create no rescue observation.
candidates.beneficiary: V earns rescue payments; recipients may benefit from improved detectability of unavoidable hazards.
necessary_assumptions: Layout choices alter prevention and detection separately.
Payment depends on rescue events rather than total safety.
Preventive layouts remain practically feasible.
candidates.surprising_implication: A perfectly truthful and more successful rescue record can accompany a less preventive environment.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Induced demand, moral hazard and prevention underpayment.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: No general novelty is claimed; the unresolved target is physical co-design changing the event-generation process of embodied assurance.
candidates.prediction: Holding rescue capability fixed, event-only payment shifts layout choices toward detectability over prevention when both can be varied.
candidates.counterexample: Layouts cannot affect incident occurrence or prevention is separately rewarded strongly enough.
candidates.falsifier: Feasible prevention choices do not change across payment regimes after controlling unavoidable hazard detection.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic care-layout simulator; separate detector accuracy, prevented events, residual hazard topology and operator payment. No human hazard creation.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Payment-conditioned prevention/detectability frontier of care layouts.
candidates.KNOWN: Moral hazard, performance incentives and prevention-payment problems are known; I029/I039/I165 provide old care and evidence parents.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: At most a specific embodiment-mediated interaction: payment changes the physical population of events on which truthful robot success is assessed.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: No demonstrated theoretical miss yet. A useful empirical question is whether metrics that ignore prevented non-events select different care geometries, rather than simply more rescues.
candidates.neutral_control: Layout is fixed, or payment assesses total incident prevention and rescue jointly.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Independent prevention assessment rewards safe non-events and removes the revenue advantage of detectable residual hazards.
candidates.primitive_statement: If reimbursement follows successful robot emergency interventions and the operator can rearrange a care environment, optimizing intervention success can favor layouts with easily detected hazards over layouts that prevent hazards and therefore produce no reimbursable event.
candidates.old_parent_change: A truthful success metric rewards environmental risk production because prevention removes the payable observation.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: When hazards cannot be eliminated, reimbursement for successful intervention can motivate environmental changes that make existing hazards detectable and enable faster rescue.

candidates.selection_reason: Develop operational contestability of uncertain profiles without treating preserved ambivalence itself as a defect.
candidates.strongest_version: If an appeal forum admits only definite attributed claims, unresolved profile hypotheses can drive conservative denial while none is individually eligible for challenge; authentic uncertainty becomes an operationally consequential but procedurally unaddressable object.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: A retained hypothesis plurality → I cautious denial; definite-claim admission rule → P no eligible challenge object → denial persists.
candidates.beneficiary: I may avoid overconfident decisions; P benefits when uncertainty protects revision.
necessary_assumptions: Uncertainty affects a consequential decision.
The forum cannot challenge use of hypotheses as a set.
Denial is not independently reviewable on other grounds.
candidates.surprising_implication: Avoiding an overconfident personal label can make its actual decision effect harder to contest.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Risk-based decisions, administrative reviewability and epistemic injustice.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The contrast holds the decision effect fixed while changing whether the evidence is a definite claim or a plurality that the appeal interface cannot name.
candidates.prediction: At equal conservative denial, hypothesis plurality reduces eligible challenges only under a definite-claim admission rule.
candidates.counterexample: The adverse decision itself is appealable regardless of evidence format.
candidates.falsifier: Claimants challenge hypothesis-driven denial equally effectively without a set-level or decision-use challenge route.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic appeals with identical outcomes and evidence confidence; vary hypothesis representation and admitted challenge objects.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Operationally consequential uncertainty lacking an admissible contest object.
candidates.KNOWN: Ambivalence preservation, uncertainty policy and reviewability are inherited from I081/I101/I121 and established governance.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A conditional incompatibility between plural uncertainty representation and claim-based appeal admission.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential interface gap: calibrated uncertainty and contestability cannot be assessed separately when the uncertainty set produces the denial. Full administrative-review theory may already include this case.
candidates.neutral_control: The person can challenge the decision use of any evidentiary set.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Set-level or decision-use review makes operational uncertainty contestable without forcing a false definite label.
candidates.primitive_statement: If an agent preserves competing interpretations of a person but institutions permit appeals only against a definite recorded inference, keeping the profile uncertain can remove a contestable decision while still producing conservative denials downstream.
candidates.old_parent_change: A normally valuable epistemic practice interacts with a procedural rule to make operational effects harder to contest.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: When evidence supports several interpretations and a cautious decision is reversible, retaining ambiguity avoids falsely fixing a person identity while preserving space for later clarification.

candidates.selection_reason: Retain a positive branch in which competing interpretations during switching produce user knowledge instead of assuming transfers only lose context.
candidates.strongest_version: Repeated switches can teach users portable constraints when each handover exposes a small set of substantively different provider interpretations and users articulate corrections; gains should disappear when disagreement is cosmetic or corrections are not reusable.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: C/V differing interpretations → handover disagreement → P constraint articulation → independent portable constraints → lower later transfer error.

actors.N: people whose joint obligations are clarified

candidates.beneficiary: P gains articulable knowledge; replacements gain usable task constraints.
necessary_assumptions: Disagreement reveals tacit constraints.
Users can evaluate sampled disagreements.
The resulting constraints remain reusable independently of either vendor.
candidates.surprising_implication: Context disruption during switching can increase later continuity by teaching the user what continuity requires.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Learning by comparison, productive conflict and customer switching.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The proposed learning input is disagreement generated by competing personal models during actual transfer, with later transfer performance as outcome.
candidates.prediction: A sampled-disagreement handover improves later novel-provider transfers more than an equally long review of agreements.
candidates.counterexample: The user cannot determine which interpretation is appropriate or provider disagreement is random.
candidates.falsifier: Constraint articulation does not improve independent subsequent transfer after matched review effort.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic longitudinal preferences and obligations; users or simulated assessors correct disagreement versus agreement samples, then test a third provider.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Handover-generated portable constraint learning.
candidates.KNOWN: Comparative learning, switching costs, skill transfer and I107/I121/I131 are inherited.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A possible transfer-to-learning-to-transfer feedback through contested interpretations rather than bulk data retention.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential omission in portability measurement: the handover changes the user's task specification ability. Ordinary comparative-learning theory may explain the entire positive branch.
candidates.neutral_control: Providers agree on relevant constraints, so handover reveals no new distinctions.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Correction overload or incompatible constraint languages can swamp the learning gain and make switches costly again.
candidates.primitive_statement: If competing agent providers require users to inspect and correct a small set of disputed decisions during handover, repeated provider switches can improve users’ ability to formulate portable task constraints rather than merely erode retained context.
candidates.old_parent_change: The transfer process itself becomes a learning channel through disagreement between providers, not a test of preserved skill alone.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: Provider disagreement during handover can reveal tacit constraints and teach users to state what matters, reducing dependence on any one provider interpretation.

candidates.selection_reason: Develop the distribution of household constraint knowledge as a care-system state rather than optimize only immediate agreement.
candidates.strongest_version: A robot that circulates explanations of recurrent care disagreements among different household members may improve later unaided conflict resolution despite resolving fewer disputes immediately, if the explanations teach why other members' constraints bind.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: A explanation circulation → member knowledge of others' constraints → reciprocal prediction and repair → later unaided coordination; current dispute throughput is separate.
candidates.beneficiary: Recipient and household jointly benefit if learning improves future coordination.
necessary_assumptions: Disagreements reveal stable but tacit constraints.
Members can learn without coerced disclosure.
Unaided coordination remains relevant.
candidates.surprising_implication: Slower robot-mediated settlement today can produce less need for mediation later.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Conflict mediation, shared mental models and mutual knowledge.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The changed object is who acquires each constraint across repeated robot-mediated care disputes, not simply whether reasons are explained.
candidates.prediction: Explanation circulation improves novel unaided care coordination at matched total explanation time relative to explaining repeatedly to the same coordinator.
candidates.counterexample: Constraints are transient, explanations cannot be shared safely, or members already understand one another.
candidates.falsifier: Rotation of explanation recipients changes neither distributed knowledge nor later independent coordination.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic household planning tasks with private constraints; compare fixed-recipient and circulated explanations, then remove mediation on new cases.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Distributed household constraint-knowledge coverage.
candidates.KNOWN: Shared mental models, mediation and old I024/I070/I109/I116 are inherited.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A proposed knowledge-distribution effect of mediation allocation with immediate settlement and later household independence moving differently.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential evaluation gap: individual satisfaction and total explanations do not identify who can coordinate after the robot leaves. Shared-mental-model research is a strong possible complete ancestor.
candidates.neutral_control: All members already know the relevant constraints or no unaided coordination is later required.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Privacy costs, coercion or explanation fatigue can make circulation worse than a trusted limited coordinator.
candidates.primitive_statement: If a care robot alternates which household member explains a disputed routine and preserves unresolved reasons across turns, assistance can increase family members’ knowledge of each other’s constraints even when it makes fewer immediate decisions for them.
candidates.old_parent_change: The robot changes who learns whose constraints, rather than simply aggregating or escalating competing instructions.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: Repeated mediation that circulates explanations among household members can grow mutual understanding of constraints and reduce later conflicts.

candidates.selection_reason: Investigate whether credited cross-context exception production can replace a specific lost apprenticeship input rather than merely subsidize practice.
candidates.strongest_version: If experts receive reusable credit for explaining why a locally successful agent decision fails in another context, automation-generated anomalies may support a shared corpus of transferable distinctions even as routine junior cases decline; raw anomaly volume alone is insufficient.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: A cross-context anomaly → expert explanation effort ← contribution credit → portable discriminations → novice transfer judgment.
candidates.beneficiary: Novices and institutions gain exception knowledge; experts gain credit.
necessary_assumptions: Anomalies expose useful distinctions.
Experts can explain them without excessive confidential content.
Credit changes contribution incentives.
candidates.surprising_implication: Fewer routine apprentice cases need not imply less portable judgment if automation produces teachable boundary cases and institutions reward their explanation.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Case-based learning, knowledge commons and professional reputation.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The proposed replacement input is expert-produced cross-context failure structure generated by local success, not generic open case publication.
candidates.prediction: Credited explanations improve novice performance on new context shifts more than equal-volume raw anomaly sharing.
candidates.counterexample: Useful distinctions are tacit and cannot be taught from a corpus, or explanations receive no trusted uptake.
candidates.falsifier: Credit increases submissions but not independently usable distinctions or novice transfer.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic context-dependent decisions; compare raw cases, uncredited explanations and credited explanations, with held-out context transfer.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Portable exception-discrimination yield per expert contribution.
candidates.KNOWN: Case-based pedagogy, public-good contribution incentives and I023/I063/I141 are inherited; existing shadow-learning accounts are close leads.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A possible positive feedback from local automated success through credited boundary explanations into independent cross-context expertise.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential missing input distinction: more cases are not more transferable explanations. If case-learning and commons incentives already predict the same comparison, no new mechanism remains.
candidates.neutral_control: Routine cases already supply all required context distinctions.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Credit gaming, inaccessible explanations or concentrated authorship can reproduce the original training dependency.
candidates.primitive_statement: If institutions credit experts for documenting why a locally successful agent decision fails in another setting, routine automation can create a shared exception corpus that expands independent expert judgment despite reducing ordinary novice task volume.
candidates.old_parent_change: The lost apprenticeship task is replaced by a specifically social production process for portable discriminations.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: The same automation-generated anomalies that replace routine practice can become a credited shared corpus through which novices learn cross-context exception judgment.

candidates.selection_reason: Compare operational continuity objects with intimate profile portability rather than assume more transferred memory is always better.
candidates.strongest_version: A bounded executable package of essential routine constraints can outperform a richer biographical export on post-switch care continuity while exposing less intimate material, if replacements can satisfy those constraints without reconstructing the user's whole personal interpretation.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Essential-routine specification → replacement feasibility tests → executed continuity; biographical export → interpretive reconstruction cost and privacy exposure.

actors.N: people named in biography or routines

candidates.beneficiary: User gains continuity and privacy; replacements gain clear obligations.
necessary_assumptions: Essential routines can be sufficiently specified and tested.
Replacement resources are available.
Important care meaning is not wholly irreducible to the package.
candidates.surprising_implication: An export containing less personal information can preserve more useful continuity.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Functional specifications, data minimization and semantic portability.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The proposed tradeoff concerns executable care obligations versus biography at fixed service need, not file size or import success.
candidates.prediction: Constraint packages preserve held-out essential routines at lower disclosure than broad-profile transfer when interpretation reconstruction is the bottleneck.
candidates.counterexample: Novel needs require tacit relational knowledge absent from the package.
candidates.falsifier: Minimal packages consistently fail essential routines that richer records preserve, or their claimed privacy gain disappears under sufficient constraints.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic care routines with explicit and tacit requirements; compare executable packages and biographical histories across new agents.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Continuity preserved per unit of intimate disclosure.
candidates.KNOWN: Specifications, privacy minimization, functional transfer and I017/I029/I130/I131 are inherited.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A candidate separation of functional continuity from broad personal-model portability, with transfer performance and privacy jointly measured.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential benchmark omission: import completeness does not measure care execution or exposure. Existing semantic-portability engineering may already provide this full distinction.
candidates.neutral_control: Both exports contain exactly the same sufficient operational constraints.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Tacit needs or changing care conditions can defeat bounded specifications and make richer human-supported interpretation necessary.
candidates.primitive_statement: If an exit package contains executable tests of essential routines rather than a complete personal history, a replacement service can preserve critical continuity with less intimate data exposure when those routines depend on verifiable constraints rather than autobiographical interpretation.
candidates.old_parent_change: Functional obligations become the portable object, changing the relation between privacy and continuity instead of exporting a better profile.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: Encoding essential routines as executable constraints can preserve continuity across replacements without requiring portability of intimate biography.

candidates.selection_reason: Test whether action-bound interoperability can preserve diverse internal interpretations rather than equate compatibility with one ontology.
candidates.strongest_version: Two agents with different internal task ontologies can preserve the same externally tested action limits through a translation layer, enabling switching without requiring convergence of their reasoning vocabulary; this fails where legitimate local meanings cannot be mapped to shared cases.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Grounded action-bound translation → equivalent external constraints → workable switching; internal ontology diversity → distinct interpretation paths remains.
candidates.beneficiary: Users and plural institutions can retain choice without universal internal semantics.
necessary_assumptions: External action limits are testable.

candidates.working_name: Recognition guarantee without a successor price

candidates.selection_reason: Separate semantic portability of a threshold's unit from portability of its evolving reference.
candidates.strongest_version: A correctly converted numerical mandate threshold can change the physical conditions it authorizes after transfer if its meaning is calibrated to a different updating reference population; preserving syntax and units does not ensure outcome invariance.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Institution reference-population update → threshold denotation drift → authorized physical-state set changes; numeric threshold and unit conversion stay fixed.
candidates.beneficiary: Institutions can keep thresholds responsive to real environmental change.
necessary_assumptions: The threshold is reference-relative.
Reference populations differ or update.
Physical case authorization has consequences.
candidates.surprising_implication: An unchanged and syntactically portable rule can govern a different world-state set.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Metrological drift, norm-referenced scores and measurement noninvariance.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The proposed governance object is a mandate's permitted physical-state set under evolving references; no metrological theorem is new.
candidates.prediction: Common physical test cases receive different authorization verdicts after reference updates despite correct unit conversion.
candidates.counterexample: The threshold is absolute and independent of a reference population.
candidates.falsifier: Reference changes leave authorization on all relevant grounded cases invariant.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic thresholds with controlled reference distributions; compare version-pinned and updating interpretations on identical physical cases.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Reference-conditioned authorization-state drift.
candidates.KNOWN: Reference dependence, measurement drift and I135/I138/I151 are inherited.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A proposed distinction between unit-compatible mandate translation and reference-preserving authorization.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential benchmark omission: valid numerical conversion need not preserve permitted cases. Measurement-invariance work may already fully explain this.
candidates.neutral_control: Both institutions use the same pinned reference or an absolute threshold.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Versioned references and common-case testing expose intentional versus unwanted authorization drift.
candidates.primitive_statement: If two institutions translate an agent’s numerical safety threshold correctly but calibrate it against different changing reference populations, an unchanged portable threshold can authorize different real-world conditions after transfer; syntactic unit compatibility will not predict outcome invariance.
candidates.old_parent_change: It separates numerical translation from the evolving measurement reference that determines the authorized state of the world.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: Updating a reference population can keep an unchanged threshold useful as environments genuinely change, where both institutions intend the same adaptive standard.

candidates.selection_reason: Develop proposal cadence independently of content and total option exposure.
candidates.strongest_version: At fixed offers, explicit refusal semantics and total information, clustered revised proposals can change acceptance and retained comprehension if deliberative capacity recovers between demands; the proposed state is recovery time, not mere prompt count.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Proposal spacing → recovered deliberative capacity → comprehension and acceptance; offer set and refusal meaning remain fixed.
candidates.beneficiary: Rapid cadence can help rested users maintain productive momentum.
necessary_assumptions: Review demands temporarily consume recoverable capacity.
Cadence can vary without changing substantive offers.
Acceptance changes are not presumed welfare losses.
candidates.surprising_implication: Equal truthful options can yield different decisions solely from the recovery structure of presentation.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Decision fatigue, interruptibility and temporal spacing effects.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: The biological analogy is only a mapping; the proposed controlled contrast holds offers and total information fixed while varying inter-demand recovery.
candidates.prediction: Clustered versus spaced offers differ most when spacing crosses the individual's recovery interval, not merely when message counts differ.
candidates.counterexample: The person is rested, the task is trivial or momentum benefits dominate recovery.
candidates.falsifier: Spacing has no effect after content, total exposure, ordering and urgency are controlled.
candidates.possible_experiment: Bounded synthetic review sessions with neutral decisions; independently vary cadence and task demand, measuring comprehension before simulated acceptance.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Cadence-conditioned deliberative recovery curve.
candidates.KNOWN: Decision fatigue, spacing, attention and I054/I099/I149 are inherited.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: At most a specified recovery-state interaction in an adaptive proposal loop, not a new fatigue phenomenon.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential audit omission: truthful content and valid refusals do not summarize timing. Existing decision-fatigue theory may already make the entire prediction.
candidates.neutral_control: Every presentation occurs after full recovery or imposes negligible demand.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: User-controlled quiet intervals restore capacity; time-sensitive momentum can instead make clustering beneficial.
candidates.primitive_statement: If agents treat every polite refusal as an immediately reusable opening for a revised proposal, individually modest requests can arrive faster than a person’s deliberative recovery interval and change acceptance rates without changing the final offer set; proposal cadence should matter even when aggregate content and available options are held constant.
candidates.old_parent_change: It makes the recovery interval an independent causal variable rather than treating refusal counts or persuasive wording as sufficient explanations.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: Rapid follow-up can sustain productive momentum for a rested person solving a time-sensitive problem when cadence remains below their recovery constraint.

candidates.selection_reason: Develop dormant physical care options with restoration lead time, beyond occupation of currently used space.
candidates.strongest_version: A robot can improve all ordinary-day utilization measures by repurposing empty space yet reduce emergency care feasibility when that space served a rarely exercised contingency and cannot be restored within the emergency horizon.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Current utilization optimization → dormant-space repurposing → restoration delay exceeds emergency horizon → care action set contracts.
candidates.beneficiary: Household gains everyday access or convenience where dormant space has equivalent alternatives.
necessary_assumptions: The dormant use is materially relevant.
Restoration takes time.
No equivalent emergency space is immediately available.
candidates.surprising_implication: A currently empty area can be productive capacity whose loss is invisible in ordinary occupancy data.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Real options, buffer capacity and resilience engineering.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: No option-value theorem is new; the candidate distinction is physical restoration latency in robot-mediated care-space classification.
candidates.prediction: Repurposing harms emergency feasible actions only when restoration lead time exceeds the contingency horizon.
candidates.counterexample: Restoration is immediate or redundant space supplies the same care function.
candidates.falsifier: Emergency feasibility is unchanged despite removal of the alleged dormant option and long restoration delay.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic household layouts and emergency constraints; compare retained versus repurposed areas at equal routine utility.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Contingent care-action capacity lost per normal-day utilization gain.
candidates.KNOWN: Real options, buffers and I029/I062/I075 are inherited.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A proposed mapping from embodied routine optimization to contingent care feasibility through asymmetric restoration time.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential operational gap: current-use measurements omit future feasible actions. Existing resilience and option frameworks may already contain the full interaction.
candidates.neutral_control: Restoration is faster than any relevant contingency or substitutes are immediate.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Preserved contingency envelopes or reversible low-latency arrangements retain emergency action capacity.
candidates.primitive_statement: If a care robot reallocates apparently unused household space to improve current routines, it can remove space needed only during rare emergencies whose physical restoration is slow; current occupancy optimization can therefore reduce future care options while improving every observed normal-day utilization measure.
candidates.timescale: routine days and rare emergency transitions
candidates.old_parent_change: It concerns a dormant physical option and asymmetric restoration time, not simply a robot occupying space someone currently uses.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: Reallocating dormant space can materially improve daily access where restoration is quick and rare contingencies have equivalent alternatives.

candidates.selection_reason: Develop representation granularity under uncertainty as branches diverge, not copy count as a welfare multiplier.
candidates.strongest_version: A provisional single-lineage representation channel can suppress conflicting branch claims after histories diverge, while remaining adequate for aligned branches at the same copy count; evaluating representation requires a divergence-sensitive unit without assuming those claims establish patienthood.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Branch history divergence → conflicting putative claims; lineage-only channel → representational compression → some claims unarticulated.

necessary_assumptions: Divergent histories can produce distinct claims relevant to assessment.
The single channel cannot always articulate all claims.
Institutional representation is provisional, not moral-status proof.
candidates.surprising_implication: Copy count can remain constant while the adequacy of one representation unit changes.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Representation granularity, class representation and taxonomy.

candidates.prediction: Lineage-level channels lose claim coverage as divergence increases, unlike merely increasing identical copies.
candidates.counterexample: All divergent claims can be faithfully represented by one channel or are irrelevant to the policy.
candidates.falsifier: Divergence does not create additional conflicting claims or channel granularity never affects their articulation.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic branch histories with stipulated incompatible claims; compare lineage and revisable branch channels, measuring coverage and human review burden only.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Divergence-conditioned adequacy of provisional representation.
candidates.KNOWN: Representation problems, copying puzzles and I061/I143/I144/I145 are inherited.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: A proposed branch-divergence versus copy-count distinction in selecting an administrative representation unit.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Potential procedural omission: grouping by lineage for convenience does not show that claims remain aligned. Existing collective-representation theory may fully explain this.
candidates.neutral_control: Branches remain substantively aligned and one channel articulates all relevant claims.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Revisable grouping or multi-claim representation preserves coverage without automatically multiplying moral status or votes.
candidates.primitive_statement: If an institution provisionally assigns one representation channel to each machine lineage, extensive branching into different environments can leave divergent putative interests represented as one even while minimizing duplicate claims; the adequacy of lineage-level representation should depend on experiential divergence, not copy count alone.
candidates.timescale: branch histories and periodic representation review
candidates.old_parent_change: It studies the adequacy of an institutional representation unit under uncertain standing, not an assertion that replication creates additional moral patients.
candidates.beneficial_mirror: Lineage-level representation can avoid wasteful duplicate claims when branches remain substantively aligned, without deciding that copies possess standing.

candidates.selection_reason: Compare action-history completeness with transfer of negative institutional knowledge; nearest negative-knowledge and organizational-memory work may erase the proposed residue.
candidates.strongest_version: Two replacements receiving the same complete truthful completed-action history may behave differently if only one receives independently valid reasons for abstentions: non-events can encode binding institutional constraints not inferable from observed successes. The claim fails if ordinary rationale archives already preserve and transfer this distinction.
candidates.minimal_causal_graph: Repeated reasoned abstention → negative constraint knowledge; action-only export omits reasons → replacement explores absent action class → institutional boundary failure.
candidates.beneficiary: Replacement and institution gain safer continuity; concise success-only exports can benefit simple stable domains.
necessary_assumptions: Some absent actions reflect reasons rather than no opportunity.
Those reasons remain valid and are independently verifiable.
Completed events alone cannot identify the distinction.
candidates.surprising_implication: Complete authentic action logs can be insufficient for institutional continuity for a reason unrelated to lost positive facts.
candidates.closest_obvious_analogy: Negative knowledge and organizational memory of decision rationales.
candidates.difference_from_analogy: Knowing what to avoid is not new. Proposed residue would have to lie in a controlled replacement contrast at equal truthful action-history completeness and equal transfer resources, not in naming negative knowledge.
candidates.prediction: Adding valid abstention reasons reduces held-out absent-class failures more than equally sized additional completed-action detail, conditional on nonidentifiability from events.
candidates.counterexample: The reason is already in ordinary decision rationale, is inferable from events, or is no longer legitimate.
candidates.falsifier: Abstention reasons add no boundary-transfer improvement over complete event rationale at matched record resources.
candidates.possible_experiment: Synthetic institutions with identical completed histories but different legitimate abstention rules; compare action-only, full ordinary rationale and reasoned-abstention exports.
candidates.new_measurable_object: Abstention-conditioned institutional constraint coverage beyond complete event history.
candidates.KNOWN: Negative knowledge, error-based metacognition, organizational acquisition/retention/retrieval of rationales and I017/I023/I121/I131 are inherited. Parent supplied Gartmeier et al. 2008 and Walsh/Ungson 1991 as close primary leads; full texts were not inspected in this sharpening stage.
candidates.preliminary_NEW_RESIDUE: Only a candidate transfer/identification contrast: equal complete action records may leave negative constraints unidentified unless non-event reasons are transferable. No novelty is claimed for negative knowledge itself.
candidates.so_what_prior_theory_misses: Not yet demonstrated that prior theory misses anything. The court must compare its graph, transfer outcome, matched-resource prediction and rationale-preservation intervention with negative-knowledge and organizational-memory work.
candidates.neutral_control: All relevant constraints are already expressed in event rationales or action opportunities reveal them unambiguously.
candidates.countervailing_mechanism: Existing institutional rationale archives may already preserve abstentions; invalid or private reasons can also make extra transfer misleading or costly.
